# roadstyle

> Python library: turn a GeoDataFrame of road edges (LineString geometry + an OSM `highway` column) into one styled, interactive, offline HTML map (MapLibre, data inlined) with road cartography (casing and fill, per-zoom widths, labels, one-way arrows, bridges and tunnels, 3D), Google Street View for the clicked road (a Street View button and floating window by default; `street_view=True` for a plain popup link, `False` for none; `rs.render_street_view` for a side-by-side page), and a `window.rs*` JavaScript API. `pip install roadstyle`; main call `rs.render_edges(gdf, ...).save("map.html")`.

Edges are directed: a two-way road is two edges with reversed geometry. JS calls (rsSelect, rsColor, rsFocus) take roadstyle feature ids from `rsQuery`, never your own `edge_id`. Unknown keywords to `render_edges` are silently ignored.

## Start here

- [Agent skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Khoshkhah/roadstyle/main/skills/roadstyle/SKILL.md): the one call, the data contract, the JS API and the traps, in one page

- [JavaScript API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Khoshkhah/roadstyle/main/docs/reference/javascript.md): every window.rs* function, every rs:* event, the registries

- [Google Street View](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Khoshkhah/roadstyle/main/docs/guides/street-view.md): the floating window (default) and the side-by-side page (beside / below)
